ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic screening shall be conducted at onboarding and on a continuous basis against the Egyptian Terrorist Entities and Terrorists List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and relevant Egyptian law enforcement and public prosecution filing lists. Domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and enhanced transaction monitoring. All screening results, risk ratings, and supporting evidence must be retained in the AML/CFT compliance file for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Invest in Egypt One-Stop Shop (OSS) company name clearance and incorporation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered name of an Egyptian LLC must be in Arabic. A Latin-script or English version may be registered as a supplementary trading name, but it must be accompanied by an approved Arabic phonetic transliteration. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered company names and protected commercial registrations in Egypt, must not be misleading, must not contravene public order or morals, and must not contain any token that implies government, military, religious, or financial licensing unless the relevant ministerial approval is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the GAFI One-Stop Shop Name Clearance Committee within 30 days from the date of the rejection notification. The appeal must include the rejection decision, a legal memorandum demonstrating distinctiveness and compliance, three alternative names, and documentary proof of any prior trademark registration relied upon. GAFI shall render a decision within 15 business days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file a judicial review petition before the Administrative Court of the State Council within 60 days from the denial. No statutory extension of a valid name reservation is available; the applicant may submit a new reservation application with the applicable fee if the 30-day window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory registered office. A physical leased or owned address located in Egypt is mandatory for the LLC incorporation filing, commercial registry listing, and issuance of the Egyptian tax card. A virtual office may be used only as an ancillary correspondence and services address after a compliant physical registered office exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate; approximately 5% to 10% annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection for a standard software and anti-cheat middleware LLC in its first operational year. The likelihood materially increases to approximately 25% or higher if the company triggers a tax audit, applies for investment incentive schemes, receives a UBO-related AML inspection, or attracts a GAFI commercial registry verification review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018) and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Article 4, Article 7, and the Chapter governing Limited Liability Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration Department and Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (عقد التأسيس والنظام الأساسي) filed electronically via GAFI and registered in the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs engaged in ISIC 6201 software and anti-cheat middleware services. The founders shall determine the capital, deposit the full amount in a licensed Egyptian bank account opened for the company under formation, and submit the bank capital certificate to GAFI. No escrow or blocked-capital account is required for non-licensed information technology services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the company is duly incorporated as EG LLC under the laws of the Arab Republic of Egypt. (2) That the subscribers' allotment of quotas in the paid-up capital, as stated in the Memorandum of Association, be and is hereby ratified and accepted. (3) That the registered office shall be located at [registered office address] and the General Authority for Investment notification shall be filed. (4) That [Name] is appointed as General Manager and [Name] as Executive Manager, each with authority to act singly to register the company, open bank accounts, and execute all documents necessary to commence business. (5) That the Corporate Secretary is instructed to file required publications and tax registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Commercial Registry Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry Office — online name reservation via gafi.gov.eg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Arabic and English company name through GAFI's electronic name reservation service. Verify that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity and that it does not contain words contrary to Egyptian public order. The system will issue a name reservation certificate valid for a limited period.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' passport or national ID copies
Draft power of attorney for a local representative, if applicable
Name reservation request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or public-policy grounds, file a written administrative appeal to GAFI Legal Affairs with three alternative proposed names within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Shahr Aqari) with GAFI preliminary legal review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association based on GAFI's standard LLC model. Ensure the articles cover registered office, capital quotas, management powers, shareholder meetings, and share/quot transfer restrictions. The founders or their legal representatives must sign before the notary, and the notary must certify the instrument. Submit the notarized draft to GAFI for legal review and clearance.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Valid passports/IDs of shareholders and managers
Foreign shareholders' corporate documents or bank references, if applicable
Statement of quota allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI requires amendments, prepare an addendum to the incorporation contract, have it notarized, and restamp the amended pages; then resubmit through the same GAFI portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the name of the company under formation and deposit the declared paid-up capital. Request a bank capital deposit certificate identifying the company, the depositors, and the amount. This certificate will be attached to the final GAFI registration file.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Draft incorporation documents and notarized signatures
Authorized signatories' passports
Tax number and anti-money-laundering declarations requested by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC documentation, supply a notarized beneficial ownership declaration and a board resolution, if available, then reapply to the same or another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final GAFI Registration, Commercial Registry Entry, and Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department and Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file via GAFI's digital portal, including the notarized incorporation contract, bank capital certificate, office lease, and all statutory declarations. Pay the prescribed registration and publication fees. GAFI will then issue the company's certificate of incorporation, assign the commercial registry extract number, and arrange legal publication in the Investment Gazette.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation file from Step 2
Bank capital deposit certificate
Lease contract of registered office
Shareholders' declarations and any required tax clearance
Payment receipt for GAFI registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises queries on the lease or foreign ownership forms, submit the original lease deed and certified Arabic translations of any foreign corporate documents within five working days via the assigned GAFI case manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Insurance, and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority, National Organization for Social Insurance, and Civil Defense Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the incorporation certificate and commercial registry extract, register the company with the Egyptian Tax Authority to obtain a Tax Identification Card. Register all employees with the National Organization for Social Insurance. If the office is in a commercial building, arrange Civil Defense fire safety inspection and obtain an occupancy/fire clearance letter from the relevant district authority.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and commercial registry extract
Copy of registered office lease
Tax registration application and board authorization
Civil Defense inspection questionnaire
Management letter confirming office occupancy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Authority delays issuance of the Tax Card beyond the statutory period, submit a formal escalation request to the Internal Complaints Unit; for Civil Defense, remedy any fire safety deficiencies and request a re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the company does not operate a physical industrial or manufacturing facility; the Ministry of Trade and Industry Industrial Development Authority is not triggered for ISIC 6201 software and anti-cheat middleware services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — software development and gaming anti-cheat middleware are non-manufacturing knowledge services; no industrial operating license is required beyond the incorporation certificate, tax registration, and commercial registry entry.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is an office-based software service with no industrial pollutant emissions; an Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to production processes; however, office operations must comply with Law No. 202 of 2020 for waste management, including responsible e-waste processing of IT hardware and no hazardous wastewater discharge or VOC emissions from office activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a Civil Defense fire safety certificate for the registered office, covering fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and electrical wiring safety. A structural load inspection is not required for standard commercial office occupancy; the lessor must provide the building occupancy permit and the Civil Defense clearance letter.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official e-tax portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; e-receipts and unified taxpayer services accessible through the ETA Integrated Tax System (Misr Digital).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must file its corporate tax registration dossier at the competent ETA tax office for the head office within 30 days of commercial registration. The LLC submits: (1) an application for the unified Tax Card on ETA forms; (2) certified copies of the Commercial Registry certificate, Memorandum of Association, board resolution appointing the tax representative, directors'/UBO passports, head-office lease, and bank account evidence; (3) the ETA then issues the permanent Tax Identification Number (TIN) used for CIT, VAT, PAYE and stamp tax; (4) VAT registration is made with the same TIN, obligated within 30 days after taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 in any rolling 12-month period; (5) the LLC must activate its e-invoicing profile, obtain an ETA digital certificate and API integrator credentials before issuing any invoice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: Egypt has no check-the-box or pass-through election; an LLC is mandatorily a resident taxpayer on worldwide taxable income at the 22.5% corporate rate. Practically available elections are: (a) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 threshold; (b) the small-business presumptive gross-receipts regime under Article 52, Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended, for qualifying taxpayers below the ministerial turnover ceiling; (c) investment incentive elections under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for qualifying projects; (d) advance tax rulings on hybrid financial instruments; no domestic hybrid-mismatch or fiscal-transparency election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies in a rolling 12-month period (mandatory registration; voluntary registration permitted below the threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA e-invoicing and e-receipts (effective phases from November 2020; Law No. 67 of 2016 and Cabinet/ETA decrees): every VAT-registered business must issue invoices through the ETA central fiscal-clearing platform using the approved XML/JSON schema, sign with the ETA digital certificate, transmit each invoice in near real time through the ETA REST API or certified ERP connector, obtain the ETA validation response, and print/embed the ETA-generated QR stamp. A non-cleared or QR-less invoice is non-compliant, bars the customer's input-VAT deduction, and attracts sanctions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Law No. 67 of 2016, exported goods and services qualify for 0% VAT. For the LLC's kernel-level anti-cheat middleware, software licenses, SaaS subscriptions and related technical support: zero-rating requires (i) the customer is non-resident with no Egyptian fixed establishment; (ii) the contract, license and support services are supplied from Egypt but consumed/used wholly outside Egypt; (iii) the supply is evidenced by a signed contract, ETA-cleared e-invoice, electronic delivery/activation logs, and an incoming foreign-currency remittance; (iv) the proceeds are repatriated to an Egyptian bank within 180 days from the supply/shipment date. Services consumed in Egypt (e.g., local gaming operators with an Egyptian establishment) remain standard-rated at 14%. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable and refundable under ETA refund procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) for physical goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency credit advice from an Egyptian bank
Signed commercial contract / purchase order identifying the non-resident customer
ETA-cleared zero-rated e-invoice bearing the ETA QR stamp
Electronic delivery and service-activation logs for software middleware
FX repatriation confirmation evidencing receipt within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audits examine export claims within the 5-year statutory limitation period, focusing on missing customs/transport evidence, absent FX remittance, related-party circular structures, or services demonstrated to be received/consumed in Egypt. Consequences of rejection: the 0% rate is reversed and 14% VAT is assessed with statutory delay interest; administrative fines run from EGP 5,000 to EGP 100,000 per non-compliant invoice and may reach 100% of the tax (up to 300% where intent to evade is proven); criminal referral to the Economic Criminal Court is possible for fraudulent export declarations, with imprisonment of responsible officers; further consequences include denial of VAT refunds, suspension of the TIN and e-invoicing profile, and personal liability of directors/shareholders in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting through the General Department of Foreign Exchange Operations and the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (MLCU), under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Banking and Financial Regulations Law) and Law No. 80 of 2002.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-driven exchange-rate system following the March 2024 liberalization. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted through authorized dealer banks for service fees, software royalties, dividends, and profit remittances, subject to documentary verification comprising audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, the Foreign Investment file registered under Law No. 72 of 2017, and underlying service contracts. Capital-account transactions, including share-capital repatriation in liquidation, require prior registration with the CBE via the authorized bank's investment application file and are executed at market rates. Practical remittance frictions include bank-level FX rationing during EGP liquidity stress, extended compliance review for indirect beneficial owners, and the 10% withholding on dividend profit remittance. For a pure software exporter with no physical goods, the risk of current-account blockage is rated Low-Medium; maintenance of a USD-denominated retention account at an authorized Egyptian bank is the recommended structural mitigation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign-exchange monitoring regulations applicable to software and services export proceeds, export receipts must be repatriated into Egypt within 5 months from the date of service performance or invoice maturity, whichever is later. Following the complete abolition of the March 2022 mandatory 100% conversion-to-EGP surrender decree as part of the 2024 exchange-rate unification, there is currently no statutory mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may retain up to 100% of export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts with authorized banks. Each receipt must be supported by the export service contract, commercial invoice, and the CBE's electronic export declaration recorded with the servicing bank. Non-repatriation within the 5-month statutory window constitutes a violation subject to CBE fines, bank account restrictions, and inclusion in the banking-sector AML exception reporting. Exporters may apply to the CBE for a one-time extension if the foreign counterparty's payment is contractually deferred, provided the deferral is commercially reasonable and documented.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and USD/EGP Operational Retention Account
Multi-Currency Operational Account with CBE investment registration
USD Operational Account and EGP Clearing Account
Non-Resident Investment Account and Cross-Border SWIFT Concentrator Account
Operational Foreign-Currency Account and Trade-Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low for onshore treasury clearing; Medium-High only as an ancillary inbound collection conduit. Under Law No. 194 of 2020, payment-service and digital-wallet operations in Egypt are CBE-licensed activities; offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Revolut hold no Egyptian payment-service license, cannot obtain a CBE settlement account, cannot issue EGP-denominated IBANs, and cannot legally clear domestic obligations. The LLC may employ a foreign EMI solely to collect inbound low-ticket payments from international gaming publishers, after which funds must be swept via SWIFT MT103 into the LLC's Egyptian authorized-bank retention account; all statutory repatriation, FX conversion, and corporate tax obligations remain with the LLC. The EMI channel must be disclosed in the AML/KYC file and onboarded as a 'downstream payment service provider' to avoid unlicensed-transfer allegations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory face-to-face compliance interview for at least one signatory or the Managing Director at the Egyptian bank branch at initial onboarding, pursuant to CBE AML/CFT regulations issued under Law No. 194 of 2020. Foreign-resident directors may delegate to an Egyptian-resident authorized signatory under a notarized power of attorney attested by the Egyptian consulate and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; most tier-one banks additionally require a live video-verification call with the foreign director. Fully remote account opening with zero physical presence and no Egyptian-resident representative is functionally unavailable for a non-resident-owned LLC under the current CBE supervisory expectations. Recommendation: appoint a local compliance-minded Egyptian manager or corporate-service provider as joint signatory to streamline onboarding and ongoing transaction approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gaming-sector keyword screen flagging potential gambling, loot-box monetization, or virtual-asset adjacency within the bank's sector-risk taxonomy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed licensing agreements with AAA game publishers proving exclusive supply of anti-cheat security middleware; written corporate self-declaration confirming zero gambling or casino exposure; ISO 27001:2022 certification and SOC 2 Type II report; ISIC 6201 trade-registry excerpt; customer due-diligence profiles of the publisher base; source-code-escrow certificate demonstrating bona fide software operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership concentration: 100% foreign shareholding with no local management presence, raising shell-company and undisclosed-control concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certified passport copies and proof-of-address documents for every ultimate beneficial owner; foreign-parent registry excerpt (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations); full organizational chart with UBO declaration form; bank reference letters from the subscribers' home banks; source-of-funds letter evidencing equity remittance via SWIFT MT103.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-base inconsistency: minimum EGP share capital relative to projected high-value software export turnover, a classic shell-company screening trigger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Actual SWIFT MT103 credit evidence of the subscribed capital; independent technology-asset valuation and patent/trademark filings; redacted master license agreements with publishing counterparties explaining the asset-light model; GAFI investment certificate; a memorandum of the Egypt expansion strategy and staffing plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border correspondent flow to emerging-market payment aggregators and gaming monetization platforms creating network-level sanctions or fraud exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant KYC pack for any Stripe/Adyen/Sportradar-style rails, including merchant IDs and processing statements; anti-fraud engine descriptions and refund-policy documentation; independent external AML risk assessment; correspondence demonstrating the LLC's active enforcement of end-user age gates and prohibited-jurisdiction filtering.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity financing must travel exclusively through an Egyptian authorized dealer bank (ADB). Protocol: (i) submit the LLC's incorporation certificate, Articles of Association, and GAFI investment registration to the ADB; (ii) open a dedicated USD Capital / Investment Account linked to the CBE's investment-record system; (iii) the foreign subscriber wires via SWIFT MT103 naming the LLC as beneficiary and using the IMF/BPM6 Purpose Code 'Direct Investment — Equity Capital' (FDI own funds) with the GAFI certificate and ISIC 6201 description in the narrative; (iv) the ADB files the CBE inward-remittance declaration, assigns an investment reference number, and either converts to EGP at the market rate or credits the USD retention account per the equity plan; (v) register the capital receipt in the LLC's share ledger and obtain the bank's confirmation to maintain the 'registered FX investment file' that is the legal precondition for future profit remittance and liquidation repatriation. Compliance verification requires the MT103/MT910 confirmation, the notarized board resolution approving the capital call, and the GAFI investment certificate. The LLC must avoid parallel-market conversion or any cash deposit of foreign currency, as unregistered inbound capital cannot be legally repatriated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the anti-cheat engine are service-dominated: cloud-hosting fees, middleware tool licenses, platform subscriptions, subcontracted research-and-development services, and inter-affiliate royalties. The standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 direct corporate wire accompanied by the head contract, commercial invoice, tax withholding certificate, and, for royalty outflows, the underlying technology-transfer registration with the CBE's current-account documentation. For physical procurement (servers, anti-DDoS appliances, hardware security modules), the preferred rail is a Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit issued by the Egyptian bank under SWIFT MT700, with a 60-to-120-day tenor, payable against Bills of Lading and commercial-invoice compliance. For domestic EGP obligations (payroll, VAT, rent, utilities), settlement runs through the Egyptian clearing systems (the Real-Time Gross Settlement and the Instant Payment Network) via the LLC's EGP operational account. All FX-disbursement instructions must reconcile against the CBE export-receipt file before execution to satisfy the bank's 'transaction visibility' requirement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP plain-vanilla forward contracts with up to 12-month tenor, strictly permitted only against documented underlying trade or service real cash-flow exposures via an authorized Egyptian bank
USD/EGP foreign-exchange swaps combining a spot sale/purchase with a matched forward contract, available from authorized dealer banks for liquidity and rollover management
USD/EGP cross-currency swaps (including floating-to-floating), permissible for monetized asset-and-liability mismatch on registered FX-denominated loans and equity capital accounts

Offshore USD/EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — available for foreign parent hedging through an international broker, but NOT permissible as an onshore corporate hedging instrument; onshore corporates must execute only deliverable instruments at CBE-authorized banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of audited annual financial statements and manager's annual report in the ordinary general assembly, including the annual dividend and audit-fee resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); approved statements and minutes are retained at the registered office and submitted to the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general assembly must be convened no later than 30 June for a 31 December financial year; approved minutes and audited financial statements are filed with the company file within 15 days of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late approval may trigger fines against the LLC managers under Companies Law No. 159/1981, invalidate dividend distributions, and obstruct tax clearance; continued default becomes a ground for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with audited financial statements, transfer-pricing disclosure, and supporting schedules for cross-border gaming anti-cheat revenue received through Swift wires and Stripe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year LLC, on or before 30 April unless an official ETA extension is issued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues additional tax of 2% per month on the unpaid tax (capped at 30%) plus interest and best-judgment assessment; prolonged non-filing may cause loss of tax-clearance status and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registration renewal of the LLC's commercial register certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, coordinated through GAFI's company registration portal where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the certificate; the renewal is completed annually by the same calendar month in which the certificate was originally issued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal gives rise to administrative late fees and suspension of the company's capacity to execute contracts, open bank accounts, or obtain import/export codes; repeated non-renewal leads to cancellation of commercial registration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the ultimate beneficial owner schedule and update of statutory registers in connection with the ordinary general assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI and the competent Egyptian AML authorities if any ownership change requires filing; otherwise the declaration is kept at the registered office and inspected by the statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The UBO schedule must be accurate as of the general-assembly date; any transfer creating direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more must be recorded within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO statements attract penalties under the Egyptian Anti-Money-Laundering Law and can result in suspension of the company's bank relationship and administrative strike-off procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit applies when the LLC's paid-up capital exceeds EGP 250,000 or when the company has non-resident shareholders, cross-border digital-services revenue, or card/payment-rails processing. The present gaming anti-cheat engine LLC qualifies because it receives Swift/Stripe payments and operates with non-resident owners, so a certified independent audit is required in all years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued under Companies Law No. 159/1981 and recognized by the Egyptian Tax Authority; EAS are substantially aligned with IFRS, and financial statements are presented in EGP or the stated functional currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each ordinary general assembly, the managers must declare that the register of members and the UBO schedule are current and accurate. A signed annual confirmation is recorded in the minutes and separately attested by the statutory auditor. Any share transfer causing a beneficial-ownership threshold of 25% or more triggers a mandatory register update within 30 days; if no transfer occurred, the existing UBO schedule is restated, dated, and approved at the annual meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Beneficial Owner Schedule

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,000 per year for a registered office in Cairo or Giza with a local compliance agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800–4,500 per year for a standard LLC with gaming anti-cheat middleware revenue and Swift/Stripe payment processing

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% of worldwide taxable profits for the Egyptian resident LLC (Article 6, Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended by Law No. 2 of 2018).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general IP box or patent box exists for ISIC 6201 middleware. Qualifying projects under Investment Law No. 72/2017 may obtain deductible investment incentives of up to 50% of invested capital. An SCZone or free-zone licensed exporter of gaming anti-cheat services may enjoy 0% CIT on foreign-source service revenue. R&D-related salary and asset depreciation deductions are available only with ETA-approved contemporaneous records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 19 (annual return, with integrated Transfer Pricing Disclosure Schedule), filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) E-TAX e-filing system and Taxpayer Services Portal (www.eta.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The ETA may assign quarterly provisional estimated returns (Form 19-A) to large taxpayers; a gaming anti-cheat middleware LLC holds annual filing status unless designated a Large Taxpayer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before four months after the fiscal year-end (Article 135, Law No. 91 of 2005); for a 31 December year-end, the filing and payment deadline is 30 April. A written discretionary extension of up to 60 days may be granted by the ETA upon request before the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total worldwide revenue from gaming anti-cheat software licenses, SaaS subscriptions, integration services, and maintenance fees; Egyptian-source and export-source revenue must be separately broken out for incentive claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company without an Egyptian permanent establishment: do not file Form 19; Egyptian-source income is finally settled by withholding at source. Non-resident with a PE: file Form 19 and report only the PE-attributable Egyptian-source profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2 - Cost of Sales and Direct Service Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs of cloud hosting, third-party game-engine licenses, subcontract labor, and directly attributable engineering costs for the anti-cheat product.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE filer: deduct only branch-attributable costs supported by ETA-validated invoices and contracts; cross-border cost allocations require TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3 - Administrative, Selling and General Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors' salaries, premises rent, professional fees, marketing, and general overhead, subject to the statutory 50% cap on entertainment and strict invoice documentation requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE filer: head-office general and administrative cost recharges are deductible only if evidenced by a binding cost-pooling agreement and an arm's-length TNMM or CUP benchmarking.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation and amortization calculated per ETA published useful-life schedules; software development intangibles cannot be self-generated and amortized unless capitalised under approved accounting and tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE filer: depreciation on assets recorded in the head-office books must be disregarded unless the assets are effectively connected to the Egyptian PE and imported per Customs and Tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 - Net Profit / Loss Before Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book profit or loss per the audited financial statements prepared under EAS/IFRS, reconciled to tax accounting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed solely from the PE's separate books and records; foreign exchange gains of the head office are not apportioned to the PE unless related to PE working capital.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Add-backs of Non-Deductible Expenditures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Over-entertainment, tax penalties, unrealized provisions, insurance of non-interested parties, remuneration paid without withholding, and all fines paid to government bodies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE filer: add back any head-office recharge exceeding arm's length, including royalties paid indirectly to the head office, which are non-deductible under Article 40(2) of law 91/2005.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct prior-year tax losses carried forward within the five-year limit; no carryback is permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not available to a non-resident filer for losses originating outside Egypt; losses of the PE that exceed Egyptian-source income are deductible only against future Egyptian-source profits of the same PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net adjusted profit subject to CIT before incentives and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Represents the PE's final taxable base subject to Article 22 of law 91/2005 for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Line 9 - Tax at Statutory Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 22.5% headline rate to the adjusted taxable income in Box 8.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same rate applies to a PE; domestic source income without a PE is subject to final WHT instead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Line 10 - Investment Incentives and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim Investment Law 72/2017 incentives, free-zone exemptions, or unilateral and treaty foreign tax credits against Egyptian corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may claim treaty credits against its home country tax only on the home-country return, not on the Egyptian return; no credit for Egyptian WHT is allowed against PE tax unless specifically provided in the treaty text.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 / Line 11 - Net Tax Payable / Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance of CIT payable with the return, net of advance payments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE, tax withheld by Egyptian customers on service revenue must be credited here against the final assessed CIT liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of controlled transactions (software licensing, SaaS, intercompany services, IP royalties, loans, and cost-sharing), tested party, TP method, profit-level indicator, and arm's length range.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for any Egyptian taxpayer with related-party transactions above the de minimis threshold; the PE's head-office group must disclose its transactions with the Egyptian branch.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a delay surcharge of 2% per month or fraction of a month on the unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the tax (Article 138, Law 91/2005). Failure to file exposes the taxpayer to an ETA default assessment based on estimated profit, fixed administrative fines, and criminal referral in cases of fraudulent concealment. Under-declaration discovered on audit also triggers the same monthly surcharge plus interest-free recalculation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% gross final withholding tax on dividends and profit distributions paid by the Egyptian LLC to a non-resident shareholder (Article 57, Law No. 91 of 2005).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) Confirm the shareholder's treaty residence and beneficial ownership of the dividend; (2) verify the treaty rate conditions, typically a minimum shareholding of 10-25% and no pass-through arrangement; (3) obtain an apostilled Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax administration for the fiscal year of the distribution; (4) submit the TRC, ownership structure chart, audited financial statements, and a formal treaty relief application to the ETA in advance of the dividend payment; (5) receive the ETA's written reduced-rate or exemption approval, apply the approved rate at source, and retain the clearance file for 5 years against a reversal on later tax audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 20% final WHT applies to royalties for software IP, patents, trademarks, and the 20% deemed-profit WHT on technical, management, and service fees paid to non-residents. Interest paid to non-resident lenders is subject to statutory 20% WHT. Under most Egyptian DTAs, reduced rates are available: typically 10-15% for royalties and 10% for bank interest, subject to the same ETA TRC clearance, beneficial ownership, and substance tests. Gaming anti-cheat license fees must be carefully characterized as royalties or service fees per the applicable DTA's software clause and the OECD commentary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million: annual aggregate value of related-party transactions (goods, services, IP royalties, interest, guarantees, and cost-sharing) that triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation under the ETA Transfer Pricing Guidelines (2021). Below this threshold, the taxpayer must still apply the arm's length principle and retain contemporaneous evidence. The Transfer Pricing Disclosure Schedule embedded in Form 19 must be filed whenever any controlled transaction exists, irrespective of the quantum.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) method - preferred for gaming software license and SaaS subscription comparables when publicly available transactions exist
Resale Price Method - applied to the distribution of bundled anti-cheat software and hardware
Cost Plus Method - used for subcontracted game-engine integration, testing, and technical support services

Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) - the most frequently applied method for the Egyptian gaming middleware tested entity, using return on total cost or operating margin as the profit-level indicator
Transactional Profit Split Method - appropriate for integrated software IP development and risk-sharing arrangements within the non-resident group
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to Gulf Cooperation Council jurisdictions. However, the general anti-avoidance rule in Article 116 of Law No. 91 of 2005, reinforced by Egyptian court doctrine, empowers the ETA to disregard any transaction, structure, or arrangement lacking genuine commercial substance and whose main purpose is tax avoidance. For a non-resident-controlled Egyptian LLC in the gaming anti-cheat sector, substantive local presence must be demonstrable through real employees under Egyptian labor contracts, payroll, actual physical office premises, technical decision-making records, board meetings in Egypt, and complete statutory books. Absent such substance, the ETA may recharacterize profits, deny treaty relief, and impute income to the economic owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically diverting Egyptian-source gaming anti-cheat license and SaaS revenue to a shell entity in a no-tax jurisdiction while the Egyptian LLC performs the actual engineering; maintaining dual accounting records; or submitting forged invoices and false transfer pricing documentation to the ETA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of two to five years plus a criminal fine of EGP 50,000 to EGP 5,000,000 under Article 144 of Law No. 91 of 2005 (as amended); mandatory recovery of the evaded CIT with the 2% monthly delay surcharge capped at 100% of the tax; asset seizure and freezing orders issued by the competent criminal court; the tax authority's right of civil recovery survives the criminal proceeding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, de facto managers, and signatories to the false returns are jointly and severally liable in personam for the evaded tax, the surcharges, and criminal fines. Conviction triggers automatic travel bans, passport seizure, placement on the ETA/CBE blacklists, and imprisonment. Egyptian courts pierce the LLC veil where the corporate form was used to commit fraud or evade tax collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Egyptian LLC as a nominal legal wrapper with no real activity, no employees, no premises, and no bank account substance, while all contracting, invoicing, and revenue settlement occur at the level of the non-resident parent or a related offshore entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the shell under Article 116 GAAR; full recharacterization of the income as attributable to the de facto beneficiary; denial of all deducted costs and losses; CIT at 22.5% on the recharacterized profit; delay surcharge of 2% per month; commercial register cancellation under Companies Law 159/1981; disqualification from contracting with Egyptian public bodies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face civil liability for the full reassessed tax, administrative debarment from board positions under the Companies Law, entry into the ETA restricted-persons registry, and travel-ban orders where the sham entity fails to settle the liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare Local File and Master File when the EGP 10 million related-party transaction threshold is exceeded; granting the non-resident group free or underpriced software IP licenses; or making no arm's-length benchmarking for intercompany SaaS, support, and SaaS platform fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA upward adjustment of the Egyptian taxable income to the arm's length value; automatic monthly delay surcharge of 2% on the differential tax (maximum 100%); administrative fine for the TP disclosure schedule deficiency; the burden of proof shifts heavily against the taxpayer when no contemporaneous documentation exists, leading to default estimation of the TP adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No criminal exposure for a pure documentation default, but the TP tax deficiency becomes a personal enforcement claim against directors if the LLC is dissolved without paying; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed at the collection stage.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterizing a management or technical service fee paid by the Egyptian LLC to the foreign parent as a 'royalty' to claim a treaty-reduced WHT rate of 0-15% where the treaty royalty rate is more favorable; or booking a share buyback as a capital gain that is not subject to the 10% dividend WHT; or artificially splitting fees to fall below WHT de minimis thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization by the ETA with full re-assessment of the under-withheld WHT at the statutory 20% or 10% rate; 2% monthly delay surcharge; a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000 for non-compliance with withholding obligations under Article 148(4) of Law 91/2005; interest and inflation adjustment of the tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Withholding agents, including the managing director and CFO, are personally liable for the full tax that should have been withheld at source. Forged TRC or benefit certificates trigger criminal exposure with imprisonment up to five years, travel bans, and ancillary asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Swift_Wire and Stripe settlement funds into foreign accounts without declaring the export of software services to the Central Bank of Egypt and the ETA; processing payments originating from sanctioned jurisdictions in final destination markets for the anti-cheat engine; or structuring inbound crowdfunding/venture payments to disguise dividend or license income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under AML Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 154 of 2021, providing for imprisonment of three to fifteen years and a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 5,000,000; forfeiture of the bank accounts and the connected proceeds; CBE license revocation for payment intermediaries; blacklisting of the company and beneficial owners from the formal banking sector.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer bear individual criminal responsibility for AML failures; they face independent imprisonment and fines even if the LLC also pays sanctions. Conviction causes automatic travel bans, removal from registered beneficial-owner lists, and lifetime prohibition from serving in any Egyptian financial institution.
